headline: Executive order updates two earlier orders on foreign intelligence surveillance to match a 2008 change to the surveillance law.
what_it_does: This order changes two earlier executive orders, 12139 and 12949, which set out how parts of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) are carried out inside the executive branch. The changes respond to the FISA Amendments Act of 2008, which Congress had recently passed. No summary was provided, so the exact changes are not described here. Based on the title, the order mainly brings the older orders in line with the new law.

who_it_affects.group: Federal intelligence and law enforcement officials
who_it_affects.how: They work under the internal rules these orders set for using foreign intelligence surveillance powers, and those rules were updated to match the 2008 law.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed October 7, 2008; the source does not state a separate start date.
